title: Espressif's Claude Code alternative knows exactly what’s connected to your ESP32
excerpt: Chat driven agents inspect performance and crash logs, iterate code, and flash a working app without a local toolchain.

Hamed holds a B.A. in English Literature, and graduated top of his class. He loves music, tech gadgets, and exploring the latest in the world of LLMs. He also enjoys tinkering with creative software such as Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and Photoshop.

Summary

  • Espressif launched ESP‑Mosaico, a modular platform for AI‑assisted, vibe‑coded ESP32 hardware projects.
  • ESP‑Claw generates and deploys device‑specific code via chat agents — no local toolchain needed.
  • Hardware‑aware agents detect peripherals, test and debug locally, reducing setup and privacy risks.

Espressif, the company behind the popular ESP32 chip, has officially launched ESP-Mosaico. It's a modular development platform specifically created for AI-assisted and vibe-coded hardware projects. Featured alongside the platform, ESP-Claw gives you a chat-based panel for using coding agents that generate code based on your specific hardware.

You tell ESP-Claw what you want the device to do, and it generates the code and deploys the application without requiring a locally configured toolchain. That makes it a tighter fit for ESP32 hardware than starting with a general-purpose agent such as Claude Code.

ESP-Claw knows what hardware it is working with

And can write the code accordingly

Many ESP32 projects come ready-made. You only have to assemble the hardware and flash the specific firmware onto the device. This popular ESP32 project, for instance, turns a Cheap Yellow Display into a surveillance detector that can identify nearby Flock cameras and Meta Glasses. However, if you have a specific idea that hasn't been done before, you'll have to write and debug the code yourself.

If you know your way around assembly code, then that's great! On the other hand, vibe coding is a great way for many DIY enthusiasts who don't necessarily have the coding knowledge to try their ideas out. That said, it's important to know what projects are simply too risky to vibe code before blindly letting AI take over your hardware, especially when the project controls motors, heat, locks, or anything safety-critical.

Thanks to ESP-Claw's hardware awareness, vibe coding an ESP32 project can be a lot more straightforward (and less risky, for sure). ESP-Mosaico can identify connected sensors, cameras, and buttons and generate an app according to your specific setup. You can also use EPS-Claw to add features or ask for alterations to existing projects.

Espressif also lets the coding agents have access to performance data and crash information, which makes debugging less of a headache. The agent can test the physical hardware and inspect the results to ensure what it produces and flashes onto your ESP32 device is actually functional. Thankfully, the interfaces, peripheral controls, and logic that don't rely on online services run locally, so you don't have to worry about your sensitive information being breached.

Thanks to ESP-Claw, bringing a custom ESP32 idea to life can be more interesting than merely installing somebody else's firmware. Given how seamlessly it integrates with your hardware, you can build these 5 popular smart home projects yourself and tweak them according to your personal use case.
